Consider setting the topic to your bootstrap_account on this one too.  I found it helpful to have the patches all grouped with the topic.

std::optional is the idiomatic way to do a transformation like this that might fail.

I also wonder if string_view should be returned here to avoid copying the role into the return value every time the function is called.  Granted they aren't big strings...

This code is removed in latest patch set and use
```
std::map<std::string, std::string> credentialRoleIdFromUserRoleId = {
    {"Administrator",
   "xyz.openbmc_project.HostInterface.CredentialBootstrapping.Role.Administrator"},
    {"Operator",
     "xyz.openbmc_project.HostInterface.CredentialBootstrapping.Role.Operator"},
    {"ReadOnly",
     "xyz.openbmc_project.HostInterface.CredentialBootstrapping.Role.ReadOnly"}};
```

please don't construct maps just do to a single lookup.  That bloats our code sizes and our memory usage.

even though it results in somewhat ugly code, please use the if/else-if ladder that's used elsewhere.
Done
setup route should always be the first thing done in a redfish method.
Done

Do we really need to support RoleId?  Our roles other than Admin are somewhat broken right now, so I'm a little surprised we'd make this configurable at all.   Was there a use case you were trying to accomplish?

The Redfish host interface spec mentions that "The permissions granted to any auto-generated credentials shall be configurable with a defined RoleId
assigned.". And the Redfish API also supported the patching to the properties of `CredentialBootstrapping` interface.

So I think the supported code needs follow spec.

Please use the appropriate helper function for these

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/a9da2b2b50758ec9657ab7034e57dadb3e62abd0/redfish-core/include/utils/dbus_utils.hpp#L54

Please fix all of them.
Done
Please capture all ec values by const reference, to avoid a copy.
Don't need to handle `ec` when using `setDbusProperty`.
Please don't duplicate this lookup.  if this struct were surviving, you would use find.
Acknowledged
